findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests; jobs, mailers, and console get "translation missing"
findings.body: The translate accelerator (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb) lazy-loads only `config.locale` inside `I18n.translate`; loading of the full fallback chain (current locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en) happens exclusively through `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, which is only invoked here in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any translation done outside the web request cycle — Sidekiq/scheduled jobs, user mailers (which render via `I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)`), rake tasks, console — with a non-default locale will have only that locale's yml files loaded. When a key is missing, the newly included `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` walks to the site default locale and then :en, but those translations were never loaded, so the lookup returns "translation missing: ..." instead of the English text. For non-English sites this means notification emails and other background-rendered content can show raw missing-translation strings — the feature this PR adds silently does nothing there. Additionally, no-argument translations are memoized in the process-wide LRU cache, so a missing-translation result produced before fallback locales are loaded can be served from cache afterwards. The fallback chain should be loaded inside the accelerator itself (e.g., in `load_locale`/`translate` or an overridden `I18n.with_locale`), not only in the controller filter.

findings.title: Fallbacks now enabled in development and test, masking missing translations
findings.body: Previously `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` existed only in the production/profile environment files. This initializer sets `I18n.fallbacks` unconditionally, so fallbacks are now active in development and test as well. In those environments a missing translation in the working locale will now silently render the English fallback instead of surfacing as a missing translation, which makes untranslated keys harder to spot during development and can let tests pass against fallback text rather than the intended translation. If that is intentional it should be called out; otherwise gate the assignment to the environments that previously had it enabled.

findings.title: No tests for the new fallback behavior
findings.body: The PR introduces a custom fallback order (requested locale → SiteSetting.default_locale → :en via `FallbackLocaleList`) and new lazy-loading of fallback locales (`I18n.ensure_loaded!`, `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!`), but adds no specs. There is no coverage asserting that a key missing in e.g. `de` resolves first to the site default locale and then to `en`, that all fallback locale files actually get loaded, or that the lazy-loading accelerator and the Fallbacks backend interact correctly. A regression spec covering those cases would protect the feature, especially given the loading is split between the initializer, the freedom patch, and the controller filter.
